Actual Article Body:
Pre-match buildup, minute by minute breakdowns and post game analysis of every Sporting Clube de Portugal match in English. Please do not confuse this as being a Sporting Lisbon site. THERE IS NO SUCH CLUB. Opinions contained within may cause laughter, offence or both. Read with caution especially when drinking.

RC Lens v Sporting CPTuesday October 13th, 2026Stade Bollaert-DelelisChampions League Matchday 2

The Warm upFrom 2012/13 onwards PSG have dominated the top flight of French football. So much so that they’ve never finished out of the top two places and only twice have they failed to be crowned champions; 2020/21 won by Lille and in 2016/17 won by AS Monaco. So last season when Lens topped Ligue 1 for 9 matchdays that age old question reared it's ugly head - they couldn't could they? No, of course they couldn't. Yet they did finish runners up which guaranteed their place in this season's Champions League. PSG rallied from their defeat in Lisboa to win back to back Champions Leagues and added another Ligue 1 title just for good measure.

Lens won their one and only Ligue 1 title in 1997/98. The iPhone was still a decade away from being launched and apple's were still something you ate for a snack or put in pies. Football clubs weren't owned by petro chemical states and the Spice Girls were en route for world domination. They were different times indeed. If you wanted to express your annoyance at your teams performances you phoned into the local radio show, wrote a letter to the Editor of the paper or had to make do with moaning to your friends. No one knew what you had for breakfast, lunch or dinner, neither would they ever look at a photo of it and the internet still needed a modem and a phone line for access.

Racing Club de Lens to give them their full name, more commonly known simply as RCL, were founded 120 years ago. Their nickname is Les Sang et Or (The Blood and Gold) based on their traditional team colours. Home is the Stade Bollaert-Delelis which was opened in the June of 1933 and boasts a capacity of 38,223.

Lens have never been associated with being one of France’s largest footballing clubs but don't confuse their runners up story from last season as being a tale of a small team overcoming massive odds with an unsuccessful title bid. They're owned by Joseph Oughourlian who has an estimated net worth of $2.5 billion. The collapse of the previous French TV rights deal when all Ligue 1 clubs were told to put €0 in their column for TV revenue may well have benefitted Lens with a billionaire owner but that's a hypothesis that may just as easily be shut down so don't quote me on that.

Oughourlian made his bid for Lens in May of 2016 against 2 further rival bids and his was given preferred status. At the time the clubs finances were described as delicate. Seems a very polite way of saying they were in dire need of financial investment and rescue but there we go, each to their own. Two months later Atlético de Madrid took a 34.6% stake in the club. By December of 2017 Oughourlian had become the sole shareholder when he bought out the minority stake held by the La Liga side.

In May of 2014 two years prior to his takeover Lens had sealed promotion back to Ligue 1. However French authorities, who really don't dick about when it comes to club finances, blocked the promotion owing to irregularities in their proposed budget. A €10m payment due from shareholder Hafiz Mammadov was missing. They appealed and won but on January 29th, 2015 it was announced they'd be relegated irrespective of where they finished.
